doc.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Williams recording with Basie and Basie's advice in Sweden
summary: Williams recalls Norman Granz at his 1955 Basie session and Basie telling him to quit while ahead before ten thousand Swedish listeners in 1956.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, I want to ask you about one other thing, too. I never forgot one thing. When I went in the studio in 1955 for Count Basie to record and I did “Every Day I have the Blues” and “Come Back” and the stuff that we did, Norman Granz, who sat in the control room and said, “ah, great, what else do you have for me?” That was his way of flattering me. “Oh that’s marvelous, what else do you have for me?” And then he turned to me and said, “remember where you made the first one,” you know. Now for me to go to Europe, I ran into some people who are here on the ship who said, “we saw you in Kurva in 1956,” Sweden, it was my first trip over, and Mr. Basie has prefaced the thing by saying, “oh you’ve been killing them in the States, haven’t you, but these people don’t understand no English. Let me see what you’re gonna do with that?” So we go out and we do what we do, “Every Day I Have the Blues” and that stuff, and there’s about ten thousand people standing on these chairs and cheering, and I said “Bas’ what are we gonna do?” He said “for once you’re gonna quit while you’re ahead.” That was Basie, you know.
